case_title: Kamal Prasad & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh (now State of Chhattisgarh)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.148; IPC s.302 r/w s.149; IPC s.307 r/w s.149; Explosive Substance Act 1908 ss.4 and 5
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW-3, PW-16, PW-17); medical and post-mortem evidence (PW-10, PW-11, PW-20)
aggravating_circumstances: Group attack by multiple persons with bombs and deadly weapons; multiple injuries to the victim on vital parts of the body
trial_court_outcome: Convicted 9 of 11 accused under IPC ss.148, 302 r/w 149, 307 r/w 149 and Explosive Substance Act ss.4/5; sentences of rigorous imprisonment for 3 years to life, concurrent (judgment dated 11.05.1992)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed (judgment dated 19.10.2010)
offence_finally_established: IPC ss.148, 302 r/w 149, 307 r/w 149; Explosive Substance Act 1908 ss.4 and 5
neutral_facts: On the morning of 17 April 1988, the victim was being taken by his son to a hospital for treatment, with a companion riding pillion. Upon reaching a particular house, eleven persons attacked them with country-made bombs, lathis and tabbal (shovels). The victim received multiple injuries and died during treatment. The companion ran off and hid in a nearby house for about two hours, suffering numerous injuries, including lacerated wounds and serious damage to his left eye. The victim's son was found alive near a tree close to the scene. He was taken to a government hospital and then to a private hospital, where he died the same day. Post-mortem examinations were performed on both bodies by two doctors. A medical officer who examined the companion opined that his lacerated wounds could have been caused by country-made bombs. The police reached the scene at about 11.15 a.m. after a report recorded at 11.00 a.m. at the companion's instance. The FIR recorded the incident time as 8.15 a.m. Three eyewitnesses, including the companion, the victim's wife and a relative of the victim, testified that the accused were present at the scene and attacked the victim with bombs, lathis and shovels. The investigating sub-inspector found the complicity of all eleven persons and filed a challan.
attempt_completion: Completed (s.307 attempt also charged, in respect of the companion)
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple bomb and blunt-weapon injuries; death of the victim's son; companion (PW-3) suffered lacerated wounds and his left eye was damaged
premeditation_planning: Not identified by the Supreme Court; the High Court (as quoted) found intention and preparation by forming an unlawful assembly
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-3, PW-16 and PW-17 placing the accused at the spot and as assailants; post-mortem and medical evidence (PW-10, PW-11, PW-20); FIR (Ex.15) and its explained delay
witness_credibility: Courts below concurrently found the witnesses truthful and inspiring confidence; Supreme Court found their testimonies coherent on material facts and the contradictions alleged not inherent; PW-3 not a relative, PW-16 a relative but not close, PW-17 the victim's wife
bail_history: Bail granted by Supreme Court order dated 01.10.2012; cancelled, appellants directed to surrender forthwith
trial_duration: offence: 17.04.1988; trial judgment: 11.05.1992; High Court: 19.10.2010; Supreme Court: 10.10.2023
legal_representation: Accused: Abhishek Vikas, Anshuman Shrivastava, Abhijeet Shrivastava, Abhishek Sharma, S. K. Verma (Advocates). State: Sumeer Sodhi, Yash Gupta (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation by SI Sahid Ali (PW-19); challan filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court (11.05.1992): convicted 9 of 11 accused. High Court (19.10.2010): appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
defence_argument: (a) inordinate delay in filing the FIR, suggesting possible improvements; (b) contradictory and unreliable prosecution witnesses; (c) the deceased was a history-sheeter with many pending cases, so someone else may have wanted him eliminated; (d) the accused were not at the scene and their alibi is probable
legal_principle_applied: Delay in FIR judged on whether the explanation is plausible on facts; alibi is a rule of evidence under s.11 Evidence Act, 1872, requiring cogent evidence and strict scrutiny; minor contradictions in eyewitness testimony not fatal; unsubstantiated claims of other enemies rejected
precedent_relied_upon: Apren Joseph v. State of Kerala (1973) 3 SCC 114; State of M.P. v. Ratan Singh (2020) 12 SCC 630; Bhagwan Singh v. Dilip Singh alias Depak (2023 SCC OnLine 1059); Binay Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (1997) 1 SCC 283; Ram Jag v. State of U.P. (1974) 4 SCC 201 (referred)
sentencing_rationale: Sentences awarded by the Trial Court and affirmed by the High Court were not excessive or disproportionate to the crimes
other_sentence_order: Bail cancelled; appellants directed to surrender forthwith; trial court to take consequential steps
